purpose: Test incremental filters, grouped evidence, sizing, ranking and their interaction under fixed tradability assumptions. Every name remains assumed accessible; financial gates are separate experimental policy choices.

policies.label: Rank and size repeat / weak close
Matched daily budget · rank and size

budget_regimes.original: No sleeve cap, reproducing the existing assumed results.
budget_regimes.matched: Same $300,000 morning gross budget and $600,000 additional-loss budget under a minimum +200% squeeze, across every policy and both slot definitions. Full parent targets remain reserved through the window.

sizing.unknown_signal: No bonus and no automatic tradeability rejection; hard-gate comparators explicitly require known passes.
sizing.shrinkage: Tier bonus times min(1, n/20), where n is distinct prior issuers in the same signal cell with entry at least 24 sessions earlier. All related distress, issuance and price signals each contribute at most one grouped point.
sizing.matched_daily: Exactly $50,000 times the number of selected parents, limited by available gross budget, allocated equally or proportionally to score-tier weights with a $100,000 per-parent ceiling. This comparison isolates reweighting from a larger intended daily capital pool.
sizing.squeeze: Risk variants use max(200%, twice the largest split-adjusted high-to-prior-close upward move in the 20 completed sessions). A $200,000 stress-loss budget caps each parent; all matched portfolios also reserve the common sleeve loss budget. Missing history retains the 200% floor, is counted, and never blocks tradeability. These are stress estimates, not guaranteed loss bounds.

validation.selection_objective: Highest min(base net P&L, stress net P&L) / max($1,000, abs(base closing drawdown), abs(stress closing drawdown)); require positive score and at least 20 completed traded issuers in each training scenario. Tie: policy identifier. Otherwise fall back to burn_100.
validation.training: Only entries and cash/loan outcomes fully completed before January 1 of the test year may score a policy. Earlier pending positions still occupy their historical admission slots. No unfinished position outcome scores selection. Base and stress training paths both use their own completed outcomes.
validation.testing: Choose before each test year, then freeze that policy for new arrivals throughout the year. Positions opened under an earlier selection retain their original size and exit. Use the identical selected plan under favorable/base/stress assumptions.
validation.issuer_tests: Replay every fixed policy without each issuer, and replay after removing its best one and five issuers. Account capacity and sizing support are recomputed. Publish aggregate robustness distributions, without per-event returns. Adaptive-plan strongest-issuer omissions recompute the annual selections; this remains retrospective research.
validation.comparisons: Run fixed-target controls, gates, sizing only, ranking only, both, shrinkage, matched daily pools, grouped versus correlated counts, and squeeze caps. Hold execution settings fixed. Report costs, actual filled capital, drawdown and concentration, not raw profit alone.
validation.status: All 2023–2026 data have already been inspected; chronological splits are retrospective and are not an untouched holdout or a live validation claim.
